topics.label: The Solar System
facts: The Solar System is the Sun and everything that travels around it, including eight planets.
The four planets closest to the Sun are rocky: Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars.
Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System.
It takes Earth about 365 days to travel once around the Sun.

questions.q: How many planets are in our Solar System?
questions.fact: The eight planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.
Jupiter is so big that more than 1,300 Earths could fit inside it.

questions.q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.fact: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun.

questions.q: Which planet do we live on?
questions.fact: Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only one known to have life.

topics.label: Gravity
facts: Gravity is a force that pulls things towards each other.
Earth's gravity pulls everything down towards the ground.
The Moon's gravity is weaker than Earth's, so astronauts can jump higher there.
Gravity keeps the Moon travelling around Earth and Earth travelling around the Sun.

choices: A force that pulls things towards each other
questions.fact: Gravity pulls objects towards each other, and bigger objects pull more strongly.

questions.q: What does Earth's gravity do to a ball you drop?
choices: It pulls it down to the ground
questions.fact: Gravity pulls the ball down towards the centre of Earth.

questions.q: Why can astronauts jump higher on the Moon?
choices: There is no air on the Moon
The Moon's gravity is weaker than Earth's
questions.fact: The Moon is smaller than Earth, so its gravity is only about one sixth as strong.

questions.q: What keeps the Moon travelling around Earth?
questions.fact: Earth's gravity keeps the Moon in orbit around our planet.

topics.label: Light
facts: Light travels in straight lines and moves incredibly fast.
Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth.
We see things because light bounces off them and into our eyes.
White light is made of many colours, which you can see in a rainbow.

questions.fact: Light travels in straight lines until it hits something or passes into a new material.

questions.q: About how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.fact: Light travels so fast that it crosses the 150 million kilometres from the Sun in about 8 minutes.

questions.q: Why can we see an object?
choices: Light bounces off it and into our eyes
The object makes its own sound
questions.fact: We see because light reflects off objects and enters our eyes.

questions.q: What colours are hidden in white light?
choices: All the colours of the rainbow
questions.fact: White light splits into red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet.

topics.label: The Planets
facts: There are eight planets in our Solar System, and Earth is the third one from the Sun.
Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest one to the Sun.
Jupiter is the largest planet, and it is bigger than all the other planets put together.
Mars looks red because its surface is covered in rusty, iron-rich dust.

questions.q: How many planets are in our Solar System?
questions.fact: There are eight planets in our Solar System.

questions.q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.fact: Mercury is the planet nearest the Sun.
Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System.

choices: Its surface is covered in rusty, iron-rich dust
It reflects the Sun's red light only
questions.fact: Mars is red because of iron-rich dust on its surface, like rust.
